title: A Classic Trap
subtitle: The pinned knight that is not pinned

steps.title: Traps in the opening
steps.source: I shall now give a few positions or traps to be avoided in the openings, and in which (practice has shown) beginners are often caught.

narration.say: Now some traps that beginners often fall into.
The black bishop on g4 pins the knight on f3 to the white queen. Or does it?

exercise.prompt: White to move. Start by taking in the centre.
exercise.success: 1. dxe5. Black takes back with the knight. He should have taken with the pawn.

steps.title: Your turn: give up the queen

narration.say: The knight on f3 is pinned to the queen. Move it anyway.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Ignore the pin.

feedback.*: The "pinned" knight can take on e5.

exercise.hint: The f3 knight takes the knight on e5.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Check with the bishop.

feedback.*: The bishop on c4 can take on f7 with check.

exercise.success: 3. Bxf7, check. Black must go to e7.

exercise.prompt: White to move and give checkmate in one.

feedback.*: The knight on c3 can give mate.

exercise.success: Checkmate, with three minor pieces against the whole black army.

narration.say: A pin to the queen is not absolute: the pinned piece can still move.
Black should have recaptured with the pawn.
